why: REFUTED AS A DOC DIVERGENCE, though the underlying security observation is real and was already on record. (1) QUOTE: verbatim, line 190 of the fetched .md. The line is two sentences; the first ('Both types execute during the same hook lifecycle.') does not reverse it. (2) EVIDENCE LINE: drifted. claude-agent.ts:301 is the closing brace of the systemPrompt object; the actual `settingSources: ['user', 'project', 'local']` is line 305, inside buildClaudeTurnShapeOptions. Content confirmed, anchor stale (older plans anchored :301 too). (3) THE REFUTATION: this page is not violated - it is satisfied. Line 84 of the same page says 'Omitting `settingSources` is equivalent to ["user", "project", "local"]', and the code comment at claude-agent.ts:302-304 says exactly that: 'Omitting this loads all three sources (CLI defaults). Spelling out the same three keeps today's behavior - including CLAUDE.md discovery, which needs project - while making the choice visible instead of implicit.' We implement the documented default verbatim, and the finding's own 'our state' text concedes that project hooks run. There is no gap against this page; the row is classified 'gap' but names no behaviour the page specifies and we lack. What it actually describes is a Nessy-internal inconsistency between two trust subsystems, which this page neither specifies nor governs. (4) ALREADY RECORDED: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-phase4-findings.md:347-350 states the identical seam under 'Two doors this unit does not close, both recorded rather than faked' - 'we pass settingSources: [user,project,local] to that SDK, so an opened repository's own .claude/settings.local.json can set outputStyle and the SDK honours it inside the preset, whatever our resolver decides. The trust gate this unit added covers our resolver and not the SDK's.' It is carried into the generated deviation register (2026-07-29-deviation-register.md:237) via the output-style-contract plan. Same door, sibling symptom (outputStyle instead of hooks). It is NOT one of the nine owner decisions in inert-worklist section 3 - I read all nine and none is this. (5) CONSEQUENCE, VERIFIED SEPARATELY FROM THE IDENTIFIER, AND IT HOLDS - so I do not refute on that ground: resolveSpawnCwd (claude-agent.ts:3045-3067) prefers session.sdkCwd, and sessions/storage.ts:200 sets `sdkCwd = options?.workingDirectory ?? getSessionDirPath(...)`, so for a project session the SDK subprocess cwd IS the opened repository. Nessy's own gate is real and does cover the same file: native-sources.ts:995 opens the trusted-only branch, and :1051-1059 reads `.claude/settings.json` / `.claude/settings.local.json` as project-scope 'permission' records inside it. And the upstream gate that could have made the consequence false does not: I disassembled the installed native binary (node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-darwin-arm64/claude). `$D()` builds the allowed-source list from the settingSources allowlist plus flagSettings/policySettings with no trust check; `kvl()` collects `hooks` from [userSettings, projectSettings, localSettings] filtered only by `allowManagedHooksOnly`; and Claude Code's own workspace-trust predicate short-circuits in SDK mode - `function fve(){if(kr())return!0;return Ip()}` with `function kr(){return!Nt.isInteractive}`, so hasTrustDialogAccepted never gates a non-interactive subprocess. The trust-boundary disagreement is therefore genuine. (6) TWO SCOPING CORRECTIONS the finding overstates: it is project sessions only - a workspace-only session gets sdkCwd = Nessy's per-session directory, and the page (line 86) says project settings.json and hooks load only from <cwd>/.claude/ with no parent-directory fallback, so no repository hooks load there; and NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE defaults OFF, which since SDK 0.2.113 means the native claude binary is not bundled, so the Claude backend cannot spawn at all in a default packaged build.
correctedState: Not a divergence from agent-sdk/claude-code-features.md. buildClaudeTurnShapeOptions (packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:305, not :301) passes settingSources: ['user', 'project', 'local'] - byte-identical to the default the same page documents at line 84 - with a comment recording the choice. Filesystem hooks from a project's .claude/settings.json consequently run in the SDK subprocess exactly as the page says they will; that is conformance, not a gap. The real content is a Nessy-internal inconsistency, and it was already recorded before this sweep: our project-trust gate (native-sources.ts:995, reading .claude/settings.json at :1051-1059 only when projectTrustState === 'trusted') governs the Nessy capability resolver, while the Claude SDK subprocess reads the same files itself with no trust check - verified in the installed native binary, where the source allowlist carries no trust predicate and Claude's own hasTrustDialogAccepted gate short-circuits to trusted whenever the session is non-interactive. docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-phase4-findings.md:347-350 states this same door for the sibling outputStyle symptom, and the deviation register carries it. Scope is narrower than claimed: project sessions only (a workspace-only session's sdkCwd is a Nessy-owned directory, and project hooks have no parent-directory fallback), and the Claude backend is off by default (NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE), which omits the native binary the subprocess needs.
